# v2.58-dev Release Notes

## Fixed: the company-scoped Offerings migration is now re-runnable

The v2.57 fix corrected the statement order, but a subtly worse problem
remained: **Prisma applies a migration without wrapping it in a transaction**, so
the *original* v2.56 failure had already committed part of its work (it added the
`offerings.company_id` column before erroring). Clearing the failed record and
retrying then tripped on the leftover column (`column "company_id" of relation
"offerings" already exists`).

The migration is now **idempotent** — every step guards on the current state
(`IF [NOT] EXISTS` / catalog checks), so it completes cleanly whether the
database is fresh, fully migrated, or left in any partial state by an earlier
failed attempt. This was verified end-to-end against a real PostgreSQL: a fresh
install, a populated database, the exact partial state left by the v2.56
failure, and a repeat run (which is now a safe no-op).

### If an earlier update attempt (v2.56 or v2.57) already failed

Your data is safe. PostgreSQL still has the migration recorded as *failed*, which
blocks new migrations, so clear that record once from the app directory (e.g.
`/opt/training-tracker`):

```bash
npx prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 20260721000000_company_scoped_offerings
```

Then run your normal update. The migration will detect and skip whatever the
earlier attempt already did and finish the rest — existing offerings are assigned
to your oldest company, with their specialisation and requirement rows preserved.
(If you have never attempted this update, no action is needed — just update.)

### Notes

- No schema or feature changes versus v2.56/v2.57 — this only makes the
  company-scoped Offerings migration safe to (re-)apply.
